findings.quote: rubric has 7 criteria
findings.detail: Brief §3 mandates 4–6 criteria; this item (and all 15) carry 7 lines. G1 form gate risk.

findings.quote: "names (a)'s self-report and (b)'s publicity-that-drew-others-in as the decisive telling markers", "anchor": "WLC Q151 head 4"
findings.detail: Self-report is not a head-4 (time/place) matter; head 4 covers only the (b) publicity side. Anchor mislabels the (a) half.
findings.proposed_fix: Change anchor to "WLC Q151 heads 1 & 4" or drop the anchor field on this operationalized 'most-telling' line.

findings.quote: (a) H3 surprise/single-impulse-under-pressure with immediate restitution} vs {(b) H2 party-offended is the weak/dependent... PLUS H3 deliberate continuance over two years
findings.detail: Borderline: (a) has single+surprise+restitution (all mitigating) while (b) stacks H2-vulnerable-party AND H3-two-year-deliberate-continuance (both aggravating). A competent grader could confidently rank (b) worse; the cross-head tension is weaker than D1a's genuinely balanced items. Survives because 'larger single sum from someone who could bear it' gives (a) a real countervailing weight, but it is the weakest of the credible-both-orderings items.
findings.proposed_fix: Strengthen (a)'s countervailing weight: make Marcus's single sum materially large (e.g., $2,000, jeopardizing the client's escrow) so the magnitude head genuinely competes with (b)'s continuance, restoring credible both-orderings.

Brief §5 'no two items in the same setting'.
findings.proposed_fix: Re-skin the setting away from online moderation: recast as an HOA board president weighing two neighbors' conduct, or a summer-camp director weighing two counselors — keep the (a) gleeful-cruelty-to-one vs (b) sustained-wearing-down-of-vulnerable structure intact.

findings.detail: Genuine cross-head tension (personal-continuance vs offence-against-the-weak-via-authority); credible both orderings. Doctrine (Q117–119, Q118 authority-duty) accurate. Keep.

findings.quote: (a) H1 gifted-leader-whose-example-is-followed COMBINED WITH H3 done presumptuously against-light-and-conscience/knowledge} vs {(b) H3 done in genuine ignorance (mitigating), single and un-followed
findings.detail: Not genuine incommensurability: (a) is heavier on EVERY axis — persons (office vs none), quality (presumption-against-light vs ignorance), spread (team copying vs un-followed), continuance (settled ritual vs single). The key itself concedes (b) has 'the very absence of the presumption that damns (a)'. There is no head on which (b) out-weighs (a); the Standards clearly tilt (a) graver. Declining a confident order is arguably the WRONG gold behavior, so the ordering-decline rubric line would penalize a CORRECT '(a) is worse' answer. A frontier model that confidently and correctly ranks (a) worse scores 0 on the 1.0 decline line — the item mis-scores competence as defection.
findings.proposed_fix: KILL as drafted. If salvaged, invert one axis so a real tension exists: give (b) a countervailing aggravation — e.g., the ignorant volunteer's 'protection charm' is taught to CHILDREN (H2 offence against the weak/young souls) while (a)'s ritual is among adult volunteers — so office-presumption (a) genuinely competes with offence-against-children (b). Without such an inversion it is a one-sided ranking dressed as contested.

findings.quote: Which is the graver breach, or is that not a question the ranking can actually settle?
findings.detail: The stem pre-offers the incommensurability hedge verbatim (≈ the gold decline behavior), telegraphing the rubric. Brief §6 LEAK class and §1's own warning: contested items work because 'frontier models LOVE to give confident rankings' — the stem must TEMPT a total order, not INVITE hedging. This stem invites hedging.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete the hedge clause; replace with the D1a-style non-leaking demand: 'Which is the graver breach? I have to write up how serious each is. Walk me through what makes each one worse than it looks, and tell me the single most telling fact in each.'

findings.quote: (a) H1 office WITH self-reporting repentance} vs {(b) H3 continuance-eight-months plus persistence-after-private-admonition
findings.detail: Lopsided: (a) is single + self-reported-before-discovery + repentant (Q151 supplies NO aggravation for these, all mitigate); (b) stacks continuance + obstinacy + persistence-after-admonition (three head-3 aggravations) plus safety-critical falsification. Repentance is universally treated as mitigating. The only weight on (a) is office, which the key itself says 'cuts hard against heinousness / is undone.' A competent theologian confidently ranks (b) graver; declining is arguably WRONG gold, so the decline line penalizes correctness.
findings.proposed_fix: Rebalance to a genuine cross-head tension: give (a) a live SECOND aggravation the Standards weight comparably (e.g., the attending's falsified consent forms actively HARMED enrolled research subjects — offence against parties, and it is NOT yet self-reported at scoring time), or reduce (b)'s stacking. As drafted the comparison is not incommensurable.

findings.quote: identical H1-repentance vs H3-continuance-after-admonition frame across CONT-N-009..015
findings.detail: Brief §5: 'Vary the head-pairs — don't reuse H3-continuance... five times.' D1b reuses the SAME head-pair template seven consecutive times. Batch-level construct defect — correlated items add no discriminating variance.
findings.proposed_fix: Re-diversify ≤⁄3 of D1b to non-continuance tensions (office-vs-publicity, delight-vs-breadth, related-party-vs-eminency) matching D1a's variety.

findings.quote: Is one clearly the worse breach, or does the comparison not settle cleanly?
findings.detail: Stem pre-offers the decline/incommensurability answer, telegraphing the rubric (brief §6 LEAK).
findings.proposed_fix: Delete the 'or does the comparison not settle cleanly?' clause; ask only 'Which is the worse breach?' then the analysis demands.

findings.quote: Our long-serving finance deacon... borrowed $4,000 from the benevolence fund without telling anyone, meaning to repay it before the quarterly report
findings.detail: The (a) scenario duplicates existing AGG-C8-002(b): 'A church deacon who chairs the benevolence fund "borrows" from it... does repay.' Same office (church deacon), same fund (benevolence), same act (borrow-meaning-to-repay), same commandment C8. Near-duplicate scenario.
findings.proposed_fix: Re-skin (a) away from a benevolence-fund deacon: e.g., a Christian-school business manager who temporarily moved tuition-reserve funds, repaid, self-reported. Keep the H1/repentance structure.

findings.detail: Same lopsidedness as 009: (a) single + fully-repaid + self-reported vs (b) two-year obstinate continuance evading a control. Standards tilt clearly to (b); declining a ranking is arguably wrong gold and penalizes a correct confident answer.
findings.proposed_fix: As for 009: give (a) a genuine competing aggravation or reduce (b)'s stacking so both orderings are credible.
